source_review: Step mode forces forks=1 before making waitChan; taskContinue reads and writes occur only in Step mode and inside the send/acquire then receive/release semaphore region, serializing all accesses.

The batch path sets forks=1 whenever Step is true, and accesses taskContinue only under Step while holding the capacity-one waitChan semaphore. Non-Step parallel execution does not access this boolean.
Step mode selects capacity-one waitChan; all taskContinue reads/writes are guarded by Step and occur between acquiring and releasing that semaphore.
The per-server batch workers access taskContinue only while Step is enabled, which sets forks=1; their waitChan send/receive region serializes those accesses.

The HTTP process is retained in bridge.httpProcess. Subsequent startup failures call bridge.Cleanup, which kills and waits both processes; success returns the bridge owner for later Cleanup.
The SOCKS process is retained in bridge.socksProcess; timeout calls Cleanup with Wait, and successful startup transfers the bridge with that cleanup method.
startLeg appends every started process to bridge.processes; later failures invoke Cleanup, which iterates that collection and kills/waits each Cmd, while success returns the owning bridge.

The branch skipping cancel requires done to close, which only happens after PeriodicallyDo returns. That function returns only when this context is canceled; the Background parent cannot cancel it independently, so the reported uncanceled early-done path is infeasible.

This negative test opens absent.db inside a newly created empty t.TempDir. OpenSQLiteFile uses SQLite OPEN_READONLY, so that missing path cannot produce a successful owned handle under the tested contract; the diagnostic assumes the intentionally rejected acquisition succeeds.

The local httptest handler only updates session state and SetCookie headers, never writes or flushes a response body. Its completed response has Content-Length zero and net/http uses NoBody, so Close releases no resource in this pinned test. Generic Close discipline is violated but the reported resource leak is vacuous; no broad HTTP/test exemption is justified.

FILE_CREATE is rejected before acquisition when ReadOnly is true. After creation, Stat failure closes f and success transfers it to the connection handle map; the later ReadOnly denial is infeasible for this creation path.

FILE_OPEN_IF creation requires ReadOnly=false because of the earlier disposition check. Stat errors close f and success transfers the handle; the later ReadOnly/delete-on-close denial cannot follow this acquisition.

Overwrite/supersede dispositions are rejected upfront in ReadOnly mode. Their acquired files are closed on Stat failure or retained in owned SMB handles; the later ReadOnly branch cannot abandon these files.
The test stores f in smbHandle.File, adds that handle to connState, and calls closeAllHandles; its sync.Map.Range callback explicitly closes each h.File before deleting entries.

panelControl registers t.Cleanup calling c.stop; stop calls pause, which invokes the current c.cancel and receives c.done. The test stores the worker cancellation and completion channel into those fields, and routes/pin also synchronously calls pause before returning; the worker is joined through the returned owner.

The constructor defers j2r.Close while isOk is false; Close waits j.cmd with a kill-timer fallback. Post-Start initialization errors invoke that cleanup, while success sets isOk and transfers the renderer owner to the caller.

The loop launches exactly two workers with distinct copied indices 0 and 1; only index 0 takes the even branch writing imgA, and the parent reads it after wg.Wait. There are not multiple writers to imgA.
Only the worker whose copied index is 1 takes the odd branch writing imgB; the fixed two-element loop and wg.Wait establish one writer followed by parent reads.

This explicit Setsid relaunch helper intentionally waits for the current PID to disappear before launching the replacement; RestartApp schedules application quit. Requiring this parent to wait for a helper that waits for parent exit contradicts the intended lifecycle.

The created file is stored in branch-assigned ioEntry.closer; handle-ID exhaustion closes that field, while success retains the entry in m.handles. Close(id) and CloseAll close the registered closer. Aggregate field ownership and error cleanup are missed.

The outer iWrapped assignment is sequenced before SwapInput publishes the new input under inputLock. The parent only launches the next iteration after receiving that iteration's uniquely tagged message through TransactionChan; this transitive mutex/channel handoff orders successive writes. err and conf are per-iteration locals. The analyzer misses the protocol-mediated serialization.
